name: Ukraine
seoTitle: History of Ukraine: Breadbasket of Europe, Blue & Yellow Flag, and 1991 Independence
metaDescription: Explore the detailed history of Ukraine. Discover Kievan Rus, the Cossack Hetmanate, the 1991 Independence referendum, and the blue-and-yellow flag.
mapFormation:
Spanning 603,628 square kilometers across Eastern Europe from the Carpathian Mountains to the Black Sea and Sea of Azov, Ukraine (Ukrayina) is the second-largest country by land area located entirely within Europe, drained by the mighty Dnieper (Dnipro) River.

The historic state originated in the 9th century with Kievan Rus centered on Kyiv, which adopted Christianity in 988 CE under Prince Volodymyr the Great. In the 16th and 17th centuries, the Zaporozhian Cossacks established the democratic Cossack Hetmanate under Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky, defending self-governing frontiers.

Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, 92.3% of Ukrainian citizens voted overwhelmingly for sovereign independence in the historic nationwide referendum of December 1, 1991, codifying Ukraine's modern sovereign frontiers.
flagHistory:
The national flag of Ukraine—the Syno-Zhovtyi Prapor—is an elegant horizontal bicolor of azure blue (top) and golden yellow (bottom), officially restored by the Verkhovna Rada on January 28, 1992.

The design was first hoisted during the 1848 Spring of Nations in Lviv. In poetic and national interpretation, Azure Blue represents the vast peaceful open skies, rivers, and mountains of Ukraine, while Golden Yellow represents the boundless golden wheat fields that make Ukraine the historic 'Breadbasket of Europe'. At the center of the national coat of arms sits the Tryzub (Trident), the ancient princely crest of Volodymyr the Great from the 10th century.
freedomStory:
Ukraine's path to modern sovereignty was forged through decades of cultural preservation and democratic revolutions.

Following the tragic artificial famine of the Holodomor (1932–1933) under totalitarian rule, Ukraine declared state sovereignty on July 16, 1990. On August 24, 1991, the Parliament passed the Act of Declaration of Independence of Ukraine (celebrated as Independence Day).

In the 21st century, Ukrainian citizens defended democratic self-determination in the 2004 Orange Revolution and the 2014 Revolution of Dignity (Euromaidan) on Kyiv's Independence Square (Maidan Nezalezhnosti), choosing a European democratic future.
challenges: Ukraine defends its sovereign territorial integrity and democratic freedom, supported by international democratic allies. Priorities include wartime defense resilience, rapid post-war reconstruction, rebuilding electrical infrastructure, and integrating into the European Union and NATO.

faqs.question: What is the Tryzub on Ukraine's coat of arms?
faqs.answer: The Tryzub (Trident) is the ancient coat of arms of Ukraine, originating as the 10th-century seal of Grand Prince Volodymyr the Great of Kievan Rus.

faqs.question: When did Ukraine declare independence?
faqs.answer: Ukraine declared independence from the Soviet Union on August 24, 1991, ratified by 92.3% of voters in a nationwide referendum on December 1, 1991.

timeline.event: Prince Volodymyr the Great Christianizes Kievan Rus, establishing European integration.
Bohdan Khmelnytsky leads the Cossack uprising, founding the Cossack Hetmanate.
The Ukrainian People's Republic declares independence following WWI.
Ukraine declares independence on August 24, confirmed by 92% of voters in referendum.
The Revolution of Dignity (Euromaidan) in Kyiv reaffirms European democratic trajectory.
